A learner of English wrote this for Reddit 提问帖（r/WarriorCats 版块） (readers: 《猫战士》粉丝社区的读者，熟悉 Darktail's Judgment 剧情的成员). What they want to do: 询问月亮石段落中星族未现身的原因并分享自己的看法.
The writer's note about it, in their words: r/WarriorCats 的提问帖。我刚开始读 Darktail’s Judgment，想问 Darkpaw 在月亮石那一段，还想说说我的看法。
The post, sentence by sentence:
<<<
[S1] I’m in the early chapters of Darktail’s Judgment, and I get a little bit confused about why StarClan didn’t show up when Darkpaw was at the moonstone and he was really miserable and furious about it.

[S2] Ravenpaw said StarClan had travelled with the Clans and left the forest skies, and it would be hard / not worth it to get back here for a distant little kittypet who wants to join the Clans.
[S3] But it was mentioned in the book that it was an overcast day, so without the moonlight it makes sense that they couldn’t reach StarClan back then when the Clans were still in the forest.
[S4] (Could someone tell me if there was a similar case in the other books where the night sky was cloudy when a cat was at the Moonstone?
[S5] Or do StarClan have the power to clear the clouds if they want to communicate?)

[S6] And Darkpaw didn’t try again on a clear day; he just chose to transform himself into Darktail👿 instead.
>>>

First summary: the post as a reader would sum it up to a friend, in two to five short lines (up to seven for a long post), in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China), in the post's order. Each line is one thing the writer does (opens, praises one thing, tells what happened, asks one thing, signs off), however many sentences it takes.
Then points: one per summary line, in the same order, and under each point the sentences that develop it as its parts. Each point with its parts covers one run of consecutive sentences: a sentence goes under the line whose run it falls in, even when it touches another line's topic.
- Every sentence goes in exactly one place. A sentence that states a point belongs to that point; the sentences that develop it (an example, a quote, the reason, a question that follows from it) are its parts. Only a sentence doing two clearly separate jobs (a quote, then a question about it) may be listed under two parts.
- When no single sentence states a point (several sentences that together praise one thing, several related questions), the point is a heading over them: sentences [] and its sentences go to its parts.
- An opening and a sign-off are points of their own (even a single word), never one point together.
- text: in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China), plain words, at most about fourteen words. What the writer says or does there ("praises how real his inner voice feels", not "inner voice"). A point with sentences of its own says only what those sentences say, not its summary line, since its parts follow right under it; a point that heads its parts (sentences []) says what they add up to. A part says only what it adds.
- kind (parts only), one of: example, quote, reason, explanation, detail, comparison, question, conclusion, context ("detail": anything else that develops the point; "context": background the point needs).
- missing: true for a part a reader here would clearly need and the post leaves out (a claim with no reason at all, a question with nothing to answer it from), with sentences [] and note: one short sentence on what the reader is left without. Only where it really matters; most posts miss nothing.
The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China).
Reply with JSON only: {"summary":[""],"points":[{"text":"","sentences":[],"parts":[{"kind":"example","text":"","sentences":[2]}]}]}
